purpose: Test whether duplicate-package detection inside one study can coexist with cross-study unlinkability and outcome-blind role separation before any real package or vendor is enrolled.

construction.keySeparation: Each study has a distinct study key. The custody key and study keys belong to different roles. Published source contains synthetic demo keys only.
construction.normalization: Synthetic package identifiers are uppercase ASCII tokens. Real deployments need an authority-controlled, versioned normalization rule and collision audit.
construction.strongerAlternative: RFC 9497 VOPRF can reduce raw-input disclosure to the PRF service, but requires a different protocol, proof verification, and implementation audit; RC32 does not implement or claim VOPRF privacy.

expectedRelations: Within each study, PACKAGE-X-FIRST equals PACKAGE-X-REPEAT.
Within each study, PACKAGE-Y-FIRST differs from both PACKAGE-X entries.
Across studies, every commitment for the same raw package differs.
No single role view contains both a raw package identifier and vendor or outcome truth.

decisionRules.acceptSyntheticQualification: All nine records obey within-study equality, within-study separation, cross-study unlinkability, view minimization, and exact view-to-public-ledger binding.
reject: raw identifier in pseudonymizer or outcome view
vendor or outcome in custody or pseudonymizer view
stopBeforeHardware: one organization controls custody and outcome truth
custody observation is not independently witnessed

hypotheses.claim: A two-stage study-scoped HMAC detects repeats within a study while preventing direct commitment equality across studies.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: Any same-study repeat differs, any different package collides, or the same raw package produces the same final commitment in two studies.

hypotheses.claim: Field-level role separation prevents any single role from joining raw identity to vendor outcome.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: Any committed role view contains both a raw package identifier or custody token and vendor or outcome truth.

hypotheses.claim: Passing the synthetic equality matrix establishes real package privacy and custody.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: The result uses public demo keys, synthetic identifiers, or no physical observation, so privacy and custody remain unqualified.

collusionBoundary: Custody and outcome roles can join records through enrollmentId if they collude. The protocol limits single-role disclosure; it is not secure multiparty computation, anonymity, or protection against two-role collusion.
safety: All identifiers, keys, vendors, outcomes, and observations are synthetic. No real serial, production key, customer record, package, or live supply-chain action is present.
